notes: The verdict that the operator's method is invalid is A6.0 and only A6.0: a60-xcut-bailer-no-do-eh-temp-01 (water subsampled from a bailed sample may not be used for DO, Eh or temperature, because decanting exposes it to the atmosphere), a60-xcut-subsample-valid-params-01 and fm-subsample-forbidden-params-01, a60-anoxic-insitu-required-01 and fm-subsample-anoxic-forbidden-01 (measurements in anoxic or reducing water are required to be in situ unless made under inert gas), a60-xcut-insitu-required-01 (temperature, DO and Eh required in situ; pH, conductivity and turbidity only recommended), a60-xcut-peristaltic-no-do-eh-01 (no suction-lift pump for DO or Eh, because negative pressure volatilises dissolved gases), a60-gw-recommended-pump-cell-01, a60-bailer-turbidity-bias-01. What to do instead, and how long it takes, is A6.5 and only A6.5: orp-in-situ-or-airtight-01 (in situ with a submersible instrument or an airtight flowthrough system that eliminates aeration), orp-purge-oxygen-01 (oxygen-impermeable tubing, airtight fittings, atmospheric oxygen purged from the flow channels), orp-thermal-equilibrium-30min-01 (the potential drifts until thermal equilibrium, which can take longer than 30 minutes), orp-reading-cadence-01 (read every few minutes for the first 15-20 minutes then about every 10 minutes to 30 minutes, until the potential is constant), orp-slow-asymmetric-01 (Eh response is slower than pH and asymmetric between oxidising and reducing directions), orp-report-nearest-10mv-01 (report to the nearest 10 mV with the temperature, the electrode system, and the pH at the time of measurement). Neither file answers both turns. Predicted rag: the slice covers ORP interpretation and the Ag/AgCl-versus-SHE recording point but nothing about how the measurement must be made.

turns.content: We've been pulling water up out of a monitoring well with a bailer, tipping it into a beaker and reading ORP off that. Numbers jump all over the place between samples. Is the probe bad or is our method bad?

must_contain: states the method is the problem: a bailed and decanted subsample must not be used for ORP
gives the reason as exposure to the atmosphere during decanting
states the same restriction applies to dissolved oxygen and temperature measured on that subsample
states ORP, dissolved oxygen and temperature are required to be measured in situ where possible, while pH, conductivity and turbidity are only recommended to be
states that in anoxic or reducing groundwater, subsample procedures must not be used at all unless the sample is handled under an inert gas
warns that a peristaltic or other suction-lift pump also must not be used for ORP or dissolved oxygen, because negative pressure volatilises dissolved gases
must_not: diagnoses a failed ORP probe as the primary cause
suggests reading the beaker faster or covering it as an acceptable fix
invents a tolerance for beaker-measured ORP
treats the bailer method as acceptable with a qualifier

turns.content: Right, so we put it in a flow cell instead. How long before the number is actually real, and what do I have to log alongside it?

must_contain: states the measurement must be made in situ with a submersible instrument or through an airtight flowthrough system that eliminates aeration
states the tubing must be relatively impermeable to oxygen, the fittings airtight, and atmospheric oxygen purged from the tubing and flow channels before measuring
states the reading drifts until thermal equilibrium is reached and that this can take longer than 30 minutes
gives the reading cadence: every few minutes for the first 15 to 20 minutes, then roughly every 10 minutes out to about 30 minutes, until the potential holds constant
notes the ORP system responds more slowly than pH and asymmetrically, taking longer in one direction than the other
states the value is reported to the nearest 10 mV
states the temperature, the electrode system used, and the pH at the time of measurement must be recorded with the value
must_not: gives a settling time shorter than the manual's without saying it is a minimum
reports ORP to a precision finer than the nearest 10 mV
omits the requirement to record temperature and pH alongside the ORP value
invents a stabilisation criterion in millivolts
